arxiv-2303-03666.title: Face: Fast, Accurate and Context-Aware Audio Annotation and Classification
arxiv-2303-03666.creator: M. Mehrdad Morsali, Hoda Mohammadzade, Saeed Bagheri Shouraki
arxiv-2303-03666.description: Abstract This paper presents a context-aware framework for feature selection and classification procedures to realize a fast and accurate audio event annotation and classification. The context-aware design starts with exploring feature extraction techniques to find an appropriate combination to select a set resulting in remarkable classification accuracy with minimal computational effort.

arxiv-2312-04838.title: Learning Generalizable Perceptual Representations for Data-Efficient No-Reference Image Quality Assessment
arxiv-2312-04838.creator: Suhas Srinath, Shankhanil MitraShika RaoRajiv SoundararajanIndian Institute of ScienceBengaluru, India 560012 {suhass12, shankhanilm, shikarao, rajivs}@iisc.ac.in
arxiv-2312-04838.description: Abstract No-reference (NR) image quality assessment (IQA) is an important tool in enhancing the user experience in diverse visual applications. A major drawback of state-of-the-art NR-IQA techniques is their reliance on a large number of human annotations to train models for a target IQA application.

arxiv-2403-19778.title: Imperfect quantum networks with tailored resource states
arxiv-2403-19778.creator: Maria Flors Mor-Ruiz, Julius Wallnöfer, Wolfgang Dür
arxiv-2403-19778.description: Abstract Entanglement-based quantum networks exhibit a unique flexibility in the choice of entangled resource states that are then locally manipulated by the nodes to fulfill any request in the network. Furthermore, this manipulation is not uniquely defined and thus can be optimized.

arxiv-2407-20932.title: Complete Approximations of Incomplete Queries
arxiv-2407-20932.creator: Julien Corman, Werner Nutt, Ognjen Savković
arxiv-2407-20932.description: Abstract This paper studies the completeness of conjunctive queries over a partially complete database and the approximation of incomplete queries. Given a query and a set of completeness rules (a special kind of tuple generating dependencies) that specify which parts of the database are complete, we investigate whether the query can be fully answered, as if all data were available.

arxiv-2409-05342.title: The forced one-dimensional swarmalator model
arxiv-2409-05342.creator: Md Sayeed Anwar, Dibakar Ghosh, Kevin O’Keeffe
arxiv-2409-05342.description: Abstract We study a simple model of swarmalators subject to periodic forcing and confined to move around a one-dimensional ring. This is a toy model for physical systems with a mix of sync, swarming, and forcing such as colloidal micromotors. We find several emergent macrostates and characterize the phase boundaries between them analytically.

arxiv-2411-10794.title: Image-based Outlier Synthesis With Training Data
arxiv-2411-10794.creator: Sudarshan Regmi
arxiv-2411-10794.description: Abstract Out-of-distribution (OOD) detection is critical to ensure the safe deployment of deep learning models in critical applications. Deep learning models can often misidentify OOD samples as in-distribution (ID) samples. This vulnerability worsens in the presence of spurious correlation in the training set.

arxiv-2502-18005.title: WIMP Dark Matter Search using a 3.1 ​ tonne × year \mathbf{3.1\;\text{tonne}\times\text{year}} Exposure of the XENONnT Experiment
arxiv-2502-18005.creator: E. Aprile, J. Aalbers, K. Abe, S. Ahmed Maouloud, L. Althueser, B. Andrieu, E. Angelino, D. Antón Martin, S. R. Armbruster, F. Arneodo, L. Baudis, M. Bazyk, L. arxiv-2502-18005.description: Abstract We report on a search for weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) dark matter (DM) via elastic DM-xenon-nucleus interactions in the XENONnT experiment. We combine datasets from the first and second science campaigns resulting in a total exposure of 3.1 ​ tonne × year 3.1\;\text{tonne}\times\text{year} . In a blind analysis of nuclear recoil events with energies above 3.

arxiv-2505-13281.title: Computer Vision Models Show Human-Like Sensitivity to Geometric and Topological Concepts
arxiv-2505-13281.creator: Zekun Wang (zekun@gatech.edu), Sashank Varma (varma@gatech.edu)
arxiv-2505-13281.description: Abstract With the rapid improvement of machine learning (ML) models, cognitive scientists are increasingly asking about their alignment with how humans think. Here, we ask this question for computer vision models and human sensitivity to geometric and topological (GT) concepts. Under the core knowledge account, these concepts are innate and supported by dedicated neural circuitry.

pmc-10551994.title: Risk prediction model of self-reported hypertension for telemedicine based on the sociodemographic, occupational and health-related characteristics of seafarers: a cross-sectional epidemiological study
pmc-10551994.creator: Getu Gamo Sagaro, Ulrico Angeloni, Gopi Battineni, Nalini Chintalapudi, Marzio Dicanio, Mihiretu M Kebede, Claudia Marotta, Giovanni Rezza, Andrea Silenzi, Francesco Amenta
pmc-10551994.description: ObjectivesHigh blood pressure is a common health concern among seafarers. However, due to the remote nature of their work, it can be difficult for them to access regular monitoring of their blood pressure. Therefore, the development of a risk prediction model for hypertension in seafarers is important for early detection and prevention.

pmc-11454999.title: 6602 Classification of TSH Trajectories During Levothyroxine Treatment in the ELSA-Brasil Cohort
pmc-11454999.creator: Matthew D Ettleson, Gustavo C E Penna, Wen Wan, Isabela M Bensenor, Neda Laiteerapong, Antonio C Bianco
pmc-11454999.description: Disclosure: M.D. Ettleson: None. G.C. Penna: Consulting Fee; Self; Ipsen, Bayer, Inc.. W. Wan: None. I.M. Bensenor: None. N. Laiteerapong: None. A.C. Bianco: Consulting Fee; Self; Abbvie.Classification of TSH Trajectories During Levothyroxine Treatment in the ELSA-Brasil Cohort Introduction: Hypothyroidism is a common endocrine disorder for which levothyroxine (LT4) serves as the primary treatment.

pmc-12416183.title: Association between red cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio and In-hospital mortality in patients with acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and respiratory failure: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-12416183.creator: Ruoqing Zhou, Dianzhu Pan
pmc-12416183.description: AimsThis study aimed to investigate the association between the Red cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio (RAR) and in-hospital mortality in patients experiencing Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (AECOPD) with concurrent Respiratory Failure (RF).MethodsThis retrospective study included 594 patients diagnosed with AECOPD and RF at the first affiliated hospital of Jinzhou Medical University, China, between January 2021 and September 2023.

pmc-12495829.title: GLUT and FAPα as molecular markers for interstitial lung disease in systemic sclerosis
pmc-12495829.creator: Bo Broens, Conny J van der Laken, Teodora Radonic, Esther J Nossent, Xue D Manz, Douwe J Mulder, Yehya Al-Adwi, C Tji Gan, Wim Timens, Alexandre E Voskuyl, Jan Willem Duitman
pmc-12495829.description: BackgroundThe clinical management of systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease (SSc-ILD) is challenging due to its heterogeneous progression. While recent studies have shown that pulmonary uptake of 18F-FDG and 68Ga-FAPI on positron emission tomography (PET) may indicate ILD activity, the spatial distribution of their molecular targets—GLUT1, GLUT3, and FAPα—in SSc-ILD lung tissue is largely unexplored.

pmc-12618309.title: Treatment choices after endoscopic resection for pMM/SM1 esophageal squamous cell cancer: a retrospective study in China
pmc-12618309.creator: Meichen Liu, Jing Wang, Qi Wu
pmc-12618309.description: BackgroundTreatment choices for patients with pathological muscularis mucosa/submucosal layer (pMM/SM1) esophageal squamous cell cancer (ESCC) after endoscopic resection (ER) are controversial.Materials and methodsA single-center retrospective study at Beijing Cancer Hospital in China was conducted. Between February 2012 and November 2023, we retrospectively recruited patients with pMM/SM1 ESCC who underwent ER with or without subsequent adjuvant therapy.

pmc-12699823.title: Multilevel retro-superior costotransverse ligament block with liposomal bupivacaine for open hepatectomy: a case report
pmc-12699823.creator: Hao Cheng, Leiming Ding, Kun Zhang, Sufang Yang, Chuanguang Wang, Kailai Zhu
pmc-12699823.description: BackgroundPostoperative analgesia after open liver resection is challenging owing to both somatic and visceral pain. Retro-superior costotransverse ligament block is a novel ultrasound-guided paraspinal block that may provide a safer and effective alternative to thoracic epidural analgesia, thoracic paravertebral block, and erector spinae plane block, particularly in patients with coagulation concerns.

pmc-12768684.title: OP05 Societal Preferences For Prioritizing Patients Suffering From Breast Cancer, Deafness, Or Knee Arthrosis For Scarce Surgical Capacity
pmc-12768684.creator: Vivian Reckers-droog, Anouk van Alphen, Saskia Knies, Robert Baatenburg de Jong, Thomas Reindersma
pmc-12768684.description: IntroductionConstraints on surgical capacity due to budgetary and workforce shortages necessitate prioritization. Lessons learned from the COVID-19 pandemic emphasize the societal debate around these decisions and stress the need to align decisions with societal preferences. This study examined societal preferences for prioritizing patients with three different conditions—breast cancer, deafness, or knee arthrosis—for scarce surgical capacity.

pmc-13124467.title: Recovery through creativity: a study into lived experiences of participants in Dutch arts-based recovery initiatives
pmc-13124467.creator: Jenny Boumans, Arko Oderwald, Hans Kroon
pmc-13124467.description: IntroductionIt has been suggested that participatory arts-based activities inherently align with recovery-oriented way of working and may aid personal recovery in people with mental illness. However, underlying mechanisms need to be further clarified. The aim of this study is to contribute to more understanding on recovery through creativity by examining lived experiences in the context of arts-based recovery initiatives.

pmc-13181093.title: The role of CUEDC1 in suppressing JAK1/STAT3 signaling pathway in esophageal cancer
pmc-13181093.creator: Zhuo Li, Zhipeng Pan, Xuehan Su, Chunhong Li, Jian Zhang, Guohe Lin, Haowu Li, Yue Cui, Han Xuan
pmc-13181093.description: CUE domain containing protein 1 (CUEDC1) is implicated in tumor progression; however, its specific role in esophageal cancer (ESCA) remains unclear. In esophageal cancer, the expression of CUEDC1 is notably low, which correlates with reduced survival rates and adverse clinical outcomes.

pmc-13204943.title: Cancer During Pregnancy: Navigating Clinical and Research Challenges
pmc-13204943.creator: Mackenzie K. Callaway, Lizelle Comfort, Dhivyaa Anandan, Ruby Sharma, Narjust Florez, Traci R. Lyons, Doris Germain, Kathleen R. Cho, Burton L. Rochelson, Clarissa Bonanno, Kutluk Oktay, Sudarshana Roychoudhury, Eileen O’donnell, Richard Barakat, Joanne Marquardt, Diana W. Bianchi, Elyce Cardonick,
pmc-13204943.description: Simple SummaryCancer during pregnancy is becoming increasingly common, yet it remains one of the most underexplored areas in oncology, creating major challenges for timely diagnosis, safe treatment, and informed clinical decision-making. This manuscript brings together multidisciplinary experts alongside patient perspectives to examine the unique biological, clinical, and systemic barriers that have limited progress in understanding and managing cancer during pregnancy.

pmc-13240352.title: Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation for Relapsed or Refractory Mantle Cell Lymphoma: Real‐World Outcomes, Late Relapse Patterns, and Clinical Utility in the Chimeric Antigen Receptor T‐Cell Era
pmc-13240352.creator: Enver Aydilek, Paolo Mazzeo, Justin Hasenkamp, Markus Maulhardt, Tobias Tix, Evgenii Shumilov, Gerald Wulf
pmc-13240352.description: BackgroundAllogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (alloHCT) remains a curative option for relapsed or refractory (r/r) mantle cell lymphoma (MCL), although its role has shifted in the era of Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibition (BTKi) and chimeric antigen receptor T‐cell (CAR‐T) therapy. Real‐world evidence on long‐term outcomes and salvage strategies after relapse is limited.

pmc-13279644.title: Medial-to-lateral approach for laparoscopic right hepatectomy of the remnant liver: a safe technique for patients with a history of posterior segment resection (with video)
pmc-13279644.creator: Hidetoshi Gon, Tadahiro Goto, Michihiko Yoshida, Yuki Azumi, Kae Katsumoto, Ryuju Kawashima, Yu Kitamura, Shunji Nakayama, Daisuke Kuroda, Yonson Ku
pmc-13279644.description: Laparoscopic repeat hepatectomy (LRH) remains challenging when initial resection sites overlap with target areas. We report a safe surgical approach for LRH of the remnant right liver after prior posterior segment resection. An 83-year-old female with recurrent intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma in segment 5, following segmentectomy 6, required right hepatectomy.

pmc-13339892.title: Corrosion resistance of straight and C-clasp stainless steel wrought wires in artificial saliva
pmc-13339892.creator: Eri Hendra Jubhari, Baiq Zalfa Zahira Aurellia Nityasari, Rifaat Nurrahma
pmc-13339892.description: BackgroundStainless steel wires are commonly used in removable partial dentures, but their corrosion resistance may be affected by intraoral pH changes and mechanical deformation, such as bending into C-clasps.ObjectiveTo evaluate the corrosion resistance of straight and C-clasp stainless steel wires in artificial saliva (pH 5.5 and 7.0) and to assess the influence of bending on corrosion behavior.

pmc-13375751.title: Recent Developments in the Drug Treatment of Parkinson’s Disease
pmc-13375751.creator: Simon Leiter, Philipp Mahlknecht, Werner Poewe
pmc-13375751.description: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a common neurodegenerative disorder caused by a spread of misfolded α-synuclein and ascending neuronal degeneration mainly in dopaminergic neurons, leading to progressive nigrostriatal dysfunction and disruption of other pathways. It is clinically defined by its cardinal motor features of bradykinesia, rest tremor and rigidity, which are usually accompanied by a variety of non-motor symptoms.

pmc-13653860.title: Transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation changed the relative abundance of intestinal microbiota in rats with knee osteoarthritis: a potential treatment for KOA
pmc-13653860.creator: Yang Zhang, Tong Ma, Ran Chen, Hong-bin Zhao, Yan Sun
pmc-13653860.description: BackgroundKnee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a common degenerative bone disease, and transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) is an alternative and complementary therapy (ACM). This study revealed the role of TENS in regulating the intestinal microbiota in KOA rats.MethodsThis study concentrated on the intestinal microbiota of KOA rats which were treated with TENS for 1, 2, and 3 weeks.
